generation.solver: converged BT solver only (duplicate-column merge + damped full-Hessian Newton, gradient gate < 1e-6 asserted on EVERY fit); the pre-convergence artifact readings are not reproducible by design
generation.stratification: S_all = 25 merged decided pairs (mixed picture caliber); S_r2 = 12 byte-faithful round-2 pairs only; S_r1 = 13 round-1 pairs only; each stratum trains on its own pairs (same-caliber training) under LOSO by topology
generation.synthetic_arms: M1s/M2s listed side by side, NEVER merged into the headline; different dose family (diagnosis card's cumulative L1-L4 caliber)

merged.overlap_note: the 3 cross-session overlap keys are tie-type in round 1 (both good), so the 25 decided pairs are disjoint

noise_baselines.gate_note: an arm counts as a signal only above the cross-session baseline 66.7% (stricter than in-session 83.3%)

M2.verdict: at the gate (equal to 2/3, not above)

epsilon_calibration.definition: full-data calibration model per arm (trained on all 25 decided pairs; synthetic added only for the s-arms); tie margin = |model score difference (M0) or BT logit (BT arms)| over the 11 both-good pairs; epsilon initial value = P75 of that distribution (P75 caliber).  The earlier epsilon0 caliber = max over tie pairs (conservative); both are reported.  Relation to the v1.3.1 review draft section 14: the feature caliber descends from its Appendix A 21-feature union, and its small-graph degeneracy risk list (gate-pinned / collapsed features) bounds what a tie margin can express - the P75 value is an INITIAL calibration constant, not a validated threshold.

fit_convergence.optimum_reference: the BT objective is convex in w (logistic loss + L2 ridge), so the asserted first-order gate ||grad|| < 1e-6 certifies a GLOBAL optimum; final objective value reported alongside

chatgpt_budget.definition_note: the 150~250 external-review budget read two ways: total ANSWERED questions vs total strict DECIDED pairs

round3_recommendation.ci_roadmap: Wilson half-width at p=0.7: n=50 -> 12.3pp, n=80 -> 9.9pp, n=100 -> 8.8pp.  An incremental verdict (M2 vs M1) needs roughly n=80~100 decided pairs in the SAME picture caliber before its CI can separate; at the pooled 61% decision yield that is about 130~165 new questions = 7~8 sessions of 20 questions.
round3_recommendation.recommendation: Round 3 = 20~24 adaptive questions with the round-2 tool, ALL rendered byte-faithful (this experiment shows the old re-routed caliber REVERSES the M2 direction, so mixing calibers again would poison the increment verdict).  Composition: M2-vs-M1 uncertain pairs first (edge-dimension increment is the open question), both-good pairs kept mixed in (epsilon calibration has only 11 samples), 3~4 cross-session retests to grow the stricter noise baseline.  jacky time per session: recorded click time was 1.5~2.5 min (median 2.7~4.0 s/question); budget 5 min with overhead.  Milestone: after ~4 sessions (~80 new answered, ~50 new decided in byte-faithful caliber) re-run this experiment; escalate to the full 150~250-pair budget only if the byte-faithful stratum keeps its direction.

sanity_flip_leg.definition: training labels deterministically half-flipped (LCG seed 20261121) on S_all; holdout pairs keep jacky's real labels; a healthy evaluator reads neither 0% nor 100%
